also: one eyewitness is worth ten hearsays
I’ll believe it when I see it

terms.latin: Plūris est oculātus testis ūnus quam aurītī decem.
terms.gloss: one witness with eyes is worth more than ten with ears
evidence: Plaut. Truc. 489: plūris est oculātus testis ūnus quam aurītī decem
terms.comment: The soldier’s maxim in the Truculentus; he goes on: those who hear tell what they have heard, those who see know for certain.
Traupman’s phrase, literally “see and believe”. We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

phrases.latin: plūris est oculātus testis ūnus quam aurītī decem; quī audiunt audīta dīcunt, quī vident plānē sciunt
phrases.english: one eyewitness is worth more than ten who have only heard; those who hear tell what they heard, those who see know for certain

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 258.
